summary: Stream replay loop causing duplicate and truncated streaming chunks for HorizonCraft during multi-region failover
description: Issue summary: Customer reported duplicate streaming chunks, truncated responses, and intermittently missing final tokens for long-running streaming completions during a cross-region failover. Impact: HorizonCraft storefront chat features returned duplicated content to end users and occasionally truncated completions; customer reported lost state for 12% of streamed requests during a two-hour window. Environment: Production (dedicated capacity) servicing HorizonCraft account across us-west primary with eu-west failover. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send a long-running streaming completion (>8s) pinned to redwood-2.0-large with session affinity; 2) Simulate a region failover by draining us-west pool (or trigger router failover); 3) Observe duplicate chunks and truncated finalization on client side. Observed logs and errors: streaming-proxy connection resets, sequence_id mismatches in serving-runtime logs, and repeated replay-receive events in the router trace. Customer impact: business-critical chat flows degraded for HorizonCraft's European user segment and Pager escalation issued. Workaround: temporary pinning of HorizonCraft to single region (eu-west) and application-level deduplication on client side were applied as mitigations.
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): collected request IDs / sample client traces and escalated to SRE. SRE findings: 1) replay logic in streaming-proxy attempted to resume streams by re-sending buffered chunks when router returned transient 502/503 during region failover; 2) when the fallback routed to a quantized model variant (redwood-2.0-quant) the KV cache prefix and sequence counters were incompatible, causing partial replays and truncated final tokens; 3) controller routing completed a two-region failover at ~2026-03-08T09:22Z aligning with a canary rollback in dedicated autoscaler (recent deploy at 2026-03-08T08:50Z). Correlated telemetry: spike in stream_replay_count and stream_duplicate_chunks, tail-latency increase for streaming tokens, and inventory mismatch on per-session cursor metrics. Evidence: traces linked in incident channel #inc-horizoncraft, dashboard panels: streaming-proxy/errors, router/replay-rate (see Confluence links). Hypothesis: a recent change in streaming-proxy to persist ephemeral stream cursors across short disconnects combined with controller's cross-region sticky routing produced amplified replays when model variant compatibility differed. Also noted a missing guard in serving-runtime for quantized-model prefix mismatch.
resolution_notes: Hotfix: rolled a targeted patch to streaming-proxy to reset ephemeral stream cursor on region/fallback boundary and to apply idempotent replay guards (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/streaming-proxy/pull/87). Additional fix added a serving-runtime guard to detect model-variant prefix incompatibility and abort graceful resume, falling back to full cold-restart of the session (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321). Rollout plan: hotfix deployed to us-west canary at 2026-03-08T11:05Z; monitored synthetic streaming workload for 30m; progressive rollout to remaining us-west nodes completed by 2026-03-08T11:55Z; eu-west rollout completed by 2026-03-08T12:45Z. Validation: post-deploy telemetry showed stream_replay_count back to baseline and duplicate chunk rate dropped to <0.1% of pre-incident traffic. Customer communication: support notified HorizonCraft of root cause and mitigation at 2026-03-08T13:00Z; offered a billing credit for the impacted window and a post-incident follow-up meeting. Follow-up actions: 1) update streaming runbook with explicit failover cursor reset steps; 2) add unit & integration tests for model-variant prefix mismatch; 3) create alerting that triggers when stream_duplicate_chunks > 0.5% for >10m; 4) schedule a dedicated post-incident review with HorizonCraft customer engineering (confluence postmortem created).
